mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 0.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their 6-month moving averages signals weakening housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall below their 6-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between INDPRO and S&P 500 returns exists: monthly increases in industrial production above 0.3% are associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting improved corporate output and earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO > 0.3% monthly change and positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns falls below 0.3 or is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample testing.
